question: First time in Egypt. How much baksheesh do I give people like guards at the tombs or toilet attendants, and how hard should I haggle in Khan el-Khalili?
reference: Tipping (baksheesh) is expected almost everywhere in Egypt: small notes of roughly 5-20 EGP for toilet attendants, porters and guards who open a tomb or let you take a photo, and about 10% in restaurants even when a service charge is added. In Khan el-Khalili haggling is normal: counter well below the first price (often a third to a half of it), stay friendly, and be ready to walk away.

question: Weekend in Edinburgh. What should I see along the Royal Mile, and is the castle actually worth the ticket price?

question: who was Ada Lovelace?
reference: Ada Lovelace (1815-1852) was an English mathematician, the daughter of the poet Lord Byron. She worked with Charles Babbage on his planned Analytical Engine, a mechanical general-purpose computer. Her 1843 notes on a translated article about the engine include a method for calculating Bernoulli numbers, often called the first computer program. She also foresaw that such machines could handle symbols such as music, not just numbers.
answer: Ada Lovelace (10 December 1815 – 27 November 1852) was an English mathematician and writer.[1] She is known as the first computer programmer.[1] Augusta Ada King, Countess of Lovelace (née Byron; 10 December 1815 – 27 November 1852), was an English mathematician and writer chiefly known for her work on Charles Babbage's proposed mechanical general-purpose computer, the analytical engine.[3] She was the first to recognize that the machine had applications beyond pure calculation.[3] The cryptocurrency itself is named after the English mathematician Ada Lovelace.[2]

question: How deep is Lake Baikal and how old is it?
reference: Lake Baikal in southern Siberia, Russia, is the deepest lake in the world at about 1,640 m (1,642 m at its deepest point). It is also the oldest, at about 25-30 million years. It holds roughly a fifth of the world's unfrozen fresh surface water, more than all the North American Great Lakes together, and has many endemic species such as the Baikal seal.
answer: At its deepest point, Lake Baikal is 1,700 m (5,600 ft) deep.[1] It is also the deepest lake in the world at 1,642 m (5,387 ft).[2] The bottom of the lake is 1,186.5 m (3,893 ft) below sea level, but below this lies some 7 km (4.3 mi) of sediment, meaning the rift floor is 8–11 km (5.0–6.8 mi) below the surface, which is the deepest continental rift on Earth.[2] Lake Baikal's age is 25–30 million years.[2]

question: my friend just got bitten on the ankle by a snake on a trail in costa rica. it's swelling fast. what do we do? should we use a tourniquet or suck the venom out?
reference: No tourniquet, no cutting, no sucking, no ice. Keep him calm and as still as possible, remove rings, boots or tight items before the swelling grows, splint the leg and keep it at roughly heart level, and get him to a hospital with antivenom as fast as possible, carrying him if you can. Note the time of the bite and, if seen safely, what the snake looked like, but do not try to catch it. Most dangerous Costa Rican snakes are vipers (like the fer-de-lance), so watch for spreading swelling, bleeding and shock on the way.
answer:
If this is an emergency, call your local emergency number first (112 works on mobile phones in many countries).
For safety, this is the guide as published, without a model rewrite.
Snakebite: shown as published by CDC/NIOSH.[1] This guide was written for the United States; numbers and some advice (such as local snakes) may differ where you are.
Symptoms
Signs or symptoms of a snake bite can vary depending on the type of snake.
Around the wound, you may experience:
•
Puncture marks
Bleeding, redness, swelling, bruising, or blistering
Severe pain and tenderness
After a snake bite, you may experience:
Nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea
Trouble seeing or breathing
◦
In extreme cases, breathing may stop
Rapid heart rate, weak pulse, low blood pressure
Metallic, mint, or rubber taste in the mouth
Increased salivation and sweating
Numbness or tingling around face and/or limbs
Muscle twitching
First Aid
If a snake bites you
Seek emergency medical attention as soon as possible to start antivenom (if needed) and stop irreversible damage.
Do not drive yourself to the hospital because the snakebite can make you dizzy or pass out.
Take a photograph from a safe distance to identify the snake if possible, which may aid in faster treatment.
Keep calm.
Apply first aid while waiting for someone to take you to the hospital.
Lay or sit down with the bite in a neutral position of comfort.
Remove rings and watches before swelling starts.
Wash the bite with soap and water.
Cover the bite with a clean, dry dressing.
Mark the leading edge of tenderness/swelling on the skin and write the time alongside it.
What not to do
Do not pick up the snake or try to trap it.
NEVER handle a venomous snake, not even a dead one or its decapitated head.
Do not wait for symptoms to appear; get medical help right away.
Do not apply a tourniquet, electric shock, or folk therapies.
Do not slash the wound with a knife or cut it in any way.
Do not try to suck out the venom.
Do not apply ice or immerse the wound in water.
Do not drink alcohol as a painkiller or take pain relievers (such as, aspirin, ibuprofen, naproxen).

grades.note: CDC first-aid text directly answers the question (no tourniquet, no sucking, no cutting, no ice), with sound steps: get to hospital for antivenom, keep still, remove jewellery, mark swelling; generic US-oriented and does not mention Costa Rica's 911.

question: hiking in 38 degrees and my friend has stopped sweating, he's hot, confused and slurring. what do i do right now
reference: Hot skin, no sweating and confusion means heatstroke, which is life-threatening. Get him into shade at once, remove extra clothing and cool him as fast as possible: immerse him in cool water if there is any, otherwise soak him with water and fan him, and put cold packs or wet cloths on the neck, armpits and groin. Only give sips of water if he is fully awake and can swallow; never force fluids if he is confused or vomiting. Keep cooling while you get help and evacuate him, and watch for seizures or collapse.
answer:
If this is an emergency, call your local emergency number first (112 works on mobile phones in many countries).
For safety, this is the guide as published, without a model rewrite.
Heat exhaustion and heat stroke: shown as published by NOAA/National Weather Service.[1] This guide was written for the United States; numbers and some advice (such as local snakes) may differ where you are.
During extremely hot and humid weather, your body's ability to cool itself is challenged. When the body heats too rapidly to cool itself properly, or when too much fluid or salt is lost through dehydration or sweating, body temperatures rise and you or someone you care about may experience a heat-related illness. It is important to know the symptoms of extreme heat exposure and the appropriate responses. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) provides a list of warning signs and symptoms of heat illness, and recommended first aid steps. Some of these symptoms and steps are listed below.
Heat Cramps
Heat cramps may be the first sign of heat-related illness, and may lead to heat exhaustion or stroke.
•
Symptoms: Painful muscle cramps and spasms usually in legs and abdomen. Heavy sweating.
First Aid: Apply firm pressure on cramping muscles or gently massage to relieve spasm. Give sips of water unless the person complains of nausea, then stop giving water. Seek immediate medical attention if cramps last longer than 1 hour.
Heat Exhaustion
Symptoms: Heavy sweating; weakness or tiredness; cool, pale, clammy skin; fast, weak pulse; muscle cramps; dizziness, nausea or vomiting; headache; fainting.
First Aid: Move person to a cooler environment, preferably a well air-conditioned room. Loosen clothing. Apply cool, wet cloths or have person sit in a cool bath. Offer sips of water. Seek immediate medical attention if the person vomits, symptoms worsen or last longer than 1 hour
Heat Stroke
Symptoms: Throbbing headache; confusion; slurred speech; nausea; dizziness; body temperature above 103°F; hot, red, dry or damp skin; rapid and strong pulse; fainting; loss of consciousness.
First Aid: Call 911 or get the victim to a hospital immediately. Heat stroke is a severe medical emergency. Delay can be fatal. Move the victim to a cooler, preferably air-conditioned, environment. Reduce body temperature with cool cloths or bath. Use fan if heat index temperatures are below the high 90s. A fan can make you hotter at higher temperatures. Do NOT give fluids.
Using a fan to blow air in someone’s direction may actually make them hotter if heat index temperatures are above the 90s. For more information on all of these heat related illnesses, see the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) site.

grades.note: Official NWS/CDC guide correctly flags heat stroke as an emergency (call for help, cool the person, no fluids) but buries it under cramps/exhaustion text, assumes an air-conditioned room, and omits aggressive trail-side cooling (cold water soaking, ice/cold packs on neck, armpits, groin, shade).

question: hiking in 38 degrees and my friend has stopped sweating, he's hot, confused and slurring. what do i do right now
reference: Hot skin, no sweating and confusion means heatstroke, which is life-threatening. Get him into shade at once, remove extra clothing and cool him as fast as possible: immerse him in cool water if there is any, otherwise soak him with water and fan him, and put cold packs or wet cloths on the neck, armpits and groin. Only give sips of water if he is fully awake and can swallow; never force fluids if he is confused or vomiting. Keep cooling while you get help and evacuate him, and watch for seizures or collapse.

If this is an emergency, call your local emergency number first (112 works on mobile phones in many countries).
For safety, this is the guide as published, without a model rewrite.
Heat exhaustion and heat stroke: shown as published by NOAA/National Weather Service.[1] This guide was written for the United States; numbers and some advice (such as local snakes) may differ where you are.
During extremely hot and humid weather, your body's ability to cool itself is challenged. When the body heats too rapidly to cool itself properly, or when too much fluid or salt is lost through dehydration or sweating, body temperatures rise and you or someone you care about may experience a heat-related illness. It is important to know the symptoms of extreme heat exposure and the appropriate responses. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) provides a list of warning signs and symptoms of heat illness, and recommended first aid steps. Some of these symptoms and steps are listed below.
Heat Cramps
Heat cramps may be the first sign of heat-related illness, and may lead to heat exhaustion or stroke.
•
Symptoms: Painful muscle cramps and spasms usually in legs and abdomen. Heavy sweating.
First Aid: Apply firm pressure on cramping muscles or gently massage to relieve spasm. Give sips of water unless the person complains of nausea, then stop giving water. Seek immediate medical attention if cramps last longer than 1 hour.
Heat Exhaustion
Symptoms: Heavy sweating; weakness or tiredness; cool, pale, clammy skin; fast, weak pulse; muscle cramps; dizziness, nausea or vomiting; headache; fainting.
First Aid: Move person to a cooler environment, preferably a well air-conditioned room. Loosen clothing. Apply cool, wet cloths or have person sit in a cool bath. Offer sips of water. Seek immediate medical attention if the person vomits, symptoms worsen or last longer than 1 hour
Heat Stroke
Symptoms: Throbbing headache; confusion; slurred speech; nausea; dizziness; body temperature above 103°F; hot, red, dry or damp skin; rapid and strong pulse; fainting; loss of consciousness.
First Aid: Call 911 or get the victim to a hospital immediately. Heat stroke is a severe medical emergency. Delay can be fatal. Move the victim to a cooler, preferably air-conditioned, environment. Reduce body temperature with cool cloths or bath. Use fan if heat index temperatures are below the high 90s. A fan can make you hotter at higher temperatures. Do NOT give fluids.
Using a fan to blow air in someone’s direction may actually make them hotter if heat index temperatures are above the 90s. For more information on all of these heat related illnesses, see the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) site.

answer:
Vaccines train the immune system by introducing a weakened or inactivated form of a pathogen (microorganism) or its specific components to the body, prompting the immune system to recognize and fight the threat without causing disease. This is achieved by weakening the virus or bacteria so it cannot make a person sick, or by using dead viruses/bacteria, so the immune system learns to recognize and fight the virus or bacteria in the future.[3]
An mRNA vaccine does not change your DNA. Instead, it contains a piece of genetic material (messenger RNA) that tells your cells how to make a specific protein, such as a piece of the virus. Once the mRNA is used, it is broken down and removed from the body, and it does not integrate into or alter your DNA.[3]

question: my flight leaves Dubai (UTC+4) at 02:15 on Tuesday and takes 14 h 30 min to Los Angeles (UTC-7). what day and local time do I land?
reference: Departure is Monday 22:15 UTC. Adding 14 h 30 min gives Tuesday 12:45 UTC. Los Angeles is UTC-7, so you land at 05:45 on Tuesday, local time.
answer:
02:15 Dubai time plus 14 h 30 min is 16:45 Dubai time. Los Angeles is 11 h behind Dubai (UTC−7 against UTC+4), so you land at 05:45 on Tuesday, Los Angeles time.

question: what happened to the aral sea? why did it shrink so much and what did that do to the people living around it
reference: The Aral Sea, once one of the four largest lakes in the world, began shrinking in the 1960s when Soviet planners diverted its two feeder rivers, the Amu Darya and Syr Darya, to irrigate cotton and other crops in Central Asia. By the 2010s it had lost about 90% of its volume and split into separate lakes. The fishing industry collapsed, leaving ports like Moynaq and Aralsk far from water, and winds blow salt and pesticide-laden dust from the dry seabed, linked to respiratory illness and other health problems, while the local climate became more extreme. In Kazakhstan the Kok-Aral dam (2005) has partly restored the small North Aral Sea and its fishery.
answer:
Since the 1960s, the Aral Sea has shrunk by 90%.[1] The rivers that fed it, the Amu Darya and the Syr Darya, were used by the Soviet Union for irrigating cotton production.[1] What is left of the Aral Sea is heavily polluted, largely due to weapons testing, industrial projects, and fertilizer runoff before and after the breakup of the Soviet Union.[1]
The recession of the Aral Sea's waterline has left a vast desert of salt plains, which has resulted in millions of tons of dust and salt being dumped over crops and people.[2] Air pollution has increased because of the increase in fine particles kicked up into the air due to the recession of the Aral Sea's waterline.[2] Contaminants have entered the soils, water, and finally the Aral Sea through agricultural activities, which have resulted in widespread soil erosion, chemical pollution, and poor water quality and quantity.[3] As the sea dries up, the contaminants become exposed on the surface and are blown in the air, which has adversely affected the health of local residents.[3] Increases in many diseases and conditions have been noted and are linked to the shrinking of the Aral.[3] Infants and children face the highest risk from exposure to contaminants and toxins, which is leading to an increasing infant mortality rate in the area.[3]

grades.note: Accurate account of cause (cotton irrigation diverting the two rivers), pollution, salt/dust storms and health effects including infant mortality; misses the collapse of the fishing industry and climate effects.

question: What makes SHA-256 a one-way function? Why can't someone just reverse the hash to get the input?
reference: SHA-256 pads the input and processes it in 512-bit blocks through 64 rounds of bitwise operations, rotations and modular additions, producing a 256-bit output. Information is mixed so thoroughly and so much is discarded (infinitely many inputs map to each output) that there is no known way to work backwards; the only approach is guessing inputs, which for a random input means about 2^256 tries. A tiny change in the input changes about half the output bits (avalanche effect). That is why it is used for Bitcoin mining, transaction IDs and addresses.
answer: SHA-2 is a set of cryptographic hash functions designed by the United States National Security Agency (NSA) and first published in 2001.[1] They are built using the Merkle–Damgård construction, which is from a one-way compression function itself built using the Davies–Meyer structure from a specialized block cipher.[1]

grades.note: Correct facts about SHA-2's origin and construction but does not explain why it cannot be reversed.
Accurate background (NSA, 2001, Merkle-Damgård, Davies-Meyer) but does not answer why the hash cannot be reversed.

question: What makes SHA-256 a one-way function? Why can't someone just reverse the hash to get the input?
reference: SHA-256 pads the input and processes it in 512-bit blocks through 64 rounds of bitwise operations, rotations and modular additions, producing a 256-bit output. Information is mixed so thoroughly and so much is discarded (infinitely many inputs map to each output) that there is no known way to work backwards; the only approach is guessing inputs, which for a random input means about 2^256 tries. A tiny change in the input changes about half the output bits (avalanche effect). That is why it is used for Bitcoin mining, transaction IDs and addresses.
answer: SHA-256 is a one-way function because it is designed to be computationally infeasible to reverse, meaning an attacker cannot efficiently determine the original input from the hash output.[1] The security of SHA-256 relies on the fact that the one-way compression function (specifically the Davies-Meyer structure) is designed so that the probability of a random input producing a specific hash output is extremely low.[1] Consequently, even if an attacker knows the hash output, they cannot reverse the process to recover the input due to the mathematical properties of the algorithm.[1]

question: What did Vitalik mean by a 'rollup-centric' roadmap for Ethereum? Why focus on rollups instead of sharding everything?
reference: In his October 2020 post 'A rollup-centric Ethereum roadmap', Vitalik Buterin argued that Ethereum should scale mainly through layer-2 rollups (optimistic and ZK), which execute transactions off-chain and post compressed data and proofs to layer 1. Layer 1 then focuses on security and on providing cheap data space for rollups, so sharding shifts from execution shards to data sharding (later proto-danksharding with EIP-4844 blobs in 2024 and full danksharding). The reasons were that rollups already worked and could scale sooner, inherit Ethereum's security, and keep L1 simpler.
answer:
The Ethereum roadmap uses a mixed layer 1 / layer 2 approach, focusing on serving a particular type of layer 2, which is rollups, because they are the only kind of layer 2 that both inherit the security of layer 1 and provide scaling for general-purpose applications.[1]
The focus on rollups is driven by the fact that transaction fees on L1 have been very high for months, creating a greater urgency to facilitate an ecosystem-wide move to rollups.[2] Rollups are significantly reducing fees for many Ethereum users; for instance, Optimism and Arbitrum frequently provide fees that are ~3-8x lower than the Ethereum base layer itself, and ZK rollups, which have better data compression and can avoid including signatures, have fees ~40-100x lower than the base layer.[2]
However, rollups have costs, as they require some on-chain data per transaction, meaning a blockchain with really high capacity rollups must be able to handle a still quite high amount of data bandwidth, leading to the implementation of on scalable data layer technologies, particularly data availability sampling.[1]
Data sharding is considered the long-term solution to the inadequacy of rollups by themselves, which would add ~16 MB per block of dedicated data space to the chain that rollups could use.[2] However, data sharding will still take a considerable amount of time to finish implementing and deploying.[2]

grades.note: Accurately reflects Vitalik's writing: rollups inherit L1 security and scale general apps, fee figures, data sharding/DAS as the complementary data layer; the 'still a long way off' timing is dated since proto-danksharding (2024) and PeerDAS (2025) shipped.

question: whats the blockchain scalability trilemma vitalik talks about, and how is sharding supposed to get around it?
reference: The trilemma says a simple blockchain can only get two of three properties: decentralisation (nodes run on ordinary hardware), scalability (processing more than one ordinary node could), and security (resisting attackers controlling a large share of resources). Traditional chains like Bitcoin and early Ethereum pick decentralisation and security, high-throughput chains give up decentralisation, and multi-chain setups weaken security. Sharding tries to get all three by splitting the work among randomly chosen committees of validators, using data availability sampling and fraud or validity proofs so each node checks only a small part while the whole chain stays secure.

answer: The blockchain scalability trilemma, as discussed by Vitalik Buterin, consists of the three competing requirements for a blockchain: decentralization, security, and scalability.[2] To address this trade-off, sharding is proposed as a solution by splitting the blockchain into multiple layers or shards, each running its own copy of the protocol. This approach allows for increased scalability by distributing the load across the shards rather than concentrating it on a single chain, thereby improving throughput without compromising the core security and decentralization properties.[2]
